---
title: "Contributing to the Wiki"
description: "How to add or update wiki pages."
---

## Quick start

1. Clone the repo: `git clone git@github.com:Omnia-Lab-UC/lab_wiki.git`
2. Create or edit a `.qmd` file in the right section folder (see below).
3. Preview locally: `quarto preview`
4. Commit and push (or open a pull request for larger changes).

## Adding a page

Create a Markdown file with a `.qmd` extension inside the section it belongs to:

```markdown
---
title: "RNA Extraction Protocol"
description: "One-line summary shown in section listings."
---

Page content in regular Markdown...
```

That's it — the sidebar and the section's index page pick up new files automatically
(except in `tutorials/`, see below).

## Ground rules

- **Language**: write in English.
- **Filenames**: lowercase kebab-case (`rna-extraction.qmd`, not `RNA Extraction.qmd`).
- **Frontmatter**: every page needs a `title` and a one-line `description`.
- **One topic per page.** Split long pages rather than growing them.
- **Never commit secrets or sensitive data.** This repo is public: no passwords, API keys, server IPs with credentials, participant data, or unpublished results.
- **Check that it renders.** Run `quarto render` before pushing; a broken page breaks the whole site build.

## Sections

| Folder | Use for |
|---|---|
| `onboarding/` | Getting started, accounts, expectations |
| `tutorials/` | Hands-on guides and courses for lab tools and workflows |
| `protocols/` | Step-by-step experimental or analysis protocols |
| `computing/` | Servers, HPC, software, environments |
| `data/` | Data management, storage, naming conventions |
| `lab-life/` | Meetings, presentations, conferences, social |

`tutorials/` works differently: it's a single page, not an auto-listed section.
To add a tutorial (or an external course), link it from `tutorials/index.qmd`;
otherwise the page gets built but isn't linked from the sidebar or any listing.

If a page doesn't fit anywhere, raise it in lab meeting before inventing a new section.
